definitions.explanation: A place where a dead person is buried; a burial site with a marker or monument.

examples.english: I visited the grave during Obon.
examples.notes: 墓を参る = to visit a grave (墓参り)

examples.japanese: ⟦{先祖|せんぞ}→先祖：04040_senzo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{墓|はか}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{京都|きょうと}→京都：09484_kyouto⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: My ancestors' graves are in Kyoto.

examples.japanese: {墓|はか}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{花|はな}→花：00523_hana⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{供|そな}えた→供える：11562_sonaeru⟧。
examples.english: I offered flowers at the grave.

examples.japanese: ⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦みんな→みんな：02972_minna⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{墓|はか}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{掃除|そうじ}→掃除：02889_souji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The whole family cleaned the grave together.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{亡|な}くなってから→亡くなる：02639_nakunaru⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、⟦{毎年|まいとし}→毎年：00731_maitoshi⟧⟦お{彼岸|ひがん}→彼岸：12612_higan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{墓|はか}{参|まい}り→墓参り：10663_hakamairi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}っている→行く：00119_iku⟧。
examples.english: Since my grandfather passed away, I visit his grave every year during the equinox.
examples.notes: ⟦お{彼岸|ひがん}→彼岸：12612_higan⟧ = equinox period (traditional time for grave visits)

notes:
USAGE: {墓|はか} refers to individual graves or tombs. In Japan, families often share a single grave marker (⟦{墓石|はかいし}→墓石：noentry⟧/⟦{墓石|ぼせき}→墓石：27326_boseki⟧).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ⟦{墓|はか}{参|まい}り→墓参り：10663_hakamairi⟧ (visiting a grave)
- {墓|はか}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{建|た}てる→建てる：01189_tateru⟧ (to erect a gravestone)
- {墓|はか}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}る→入る：00494_hairu⟧ (to be buried)
- {墓|はか}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{掃除|そうじ}→掃除：02889_souji⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to clean the grave)

COMPOUNDS:
- ⟦{墓|はか}{参|まい}り→墓参り：10663_hakamairi⟧ (grave visit)
- ⟦{墓地|ぼち}→墓地：15232_bochi⟧ (cemetery, graveyard)
- ⟦{墓石|はかいし}→墓石：noentry⟧/⟦{墓石|ぼせき}→墓石：27326_boseki⟧ (gravestone, tombstone)
- ⟦{墓場|はかば}→墓場：05876_hakaba⟧ (graveyard)
- ⟦お{墓|はか}→お墓：21734_ohaka⟧ (grave - polite)

CULTURAL NOTE: Visiting family graves (⟦{墓参|はかまい}り→墓参り：10663_hakamairi⟧) is an important tradition in Japan, especially during ⟦お{盆|ぼん}→お盆：05587_obon⟧ (Obon) and ⟦お{彼岸|ひがん}→彼岸：12612_higan⟧ (equinox periods).
